thread:
lina_support: FYI customer novaai reporting sustained 429s and P95 latency spikes from their Dedicated pool around 09:10 UTC. they say traffic landed on `shared-overflow` instead of their `novaai-gold` pool.

omar_runtime: can you paste a sample request from their SDK logs?

lina_support: redacted curl they provided:

`````
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer <token>\" \
  -H \"X-Redwood-Tenant: novaai\" \
  -H \"X-Redwood-Tier: [\"gold\",\"canary\"]\" \
  -d '{\"prompt\":\"summarize\"}'
`````

lina_support: response body: {\"error\":\"rate_limit_exceeded\",\"pool\":\"shared-overflow\"}

omar_runtime: interesting. looks like their SDK serializes tier list as a JSON array literal in the header; in this case parse succeeded but downstream matcher expected plain aliases like `gold` and treated the parsed array as a single token list -> no matching pool -> fallback.

becky_ops: confirmed in controlplane logs at 09:09:58:

`````
[09:09:58] route.parse header_tier='[\"gold\",\"canary\"]' -> parsed_as_array [\"gold\",\"canary\"]
[09:09:58] route.match tenant=novaai tiers=[[\"gold\",\"canary\"]] -> no match
[09:09:58] route.fallback -> pool=shared-overflow
[09:09:58] quota.check pool=shared-overflow -> exceeded -> 429
`````

kevin_sre: because requests never hit `novaai-gold` autoscaler metrics stayed low and no scale-up happened. shared-overflow got noisy neighbors which tripped rate limits.

maya_product: novaai is on a Gold dedicated contract. CSM escalated; they want an immediate workaround and ETA for fix. ops: can you apply a tenant override?

becky_ops: yes I can add tenant mapping novaai -> novaai-gold in controlplane. will do with canary verification.

sre-bot: :warning: alert: increased 429s for pool=shared-overflow (src=controlplane-routing) window 09:05-09:25 UTC

omar_runtime: short-term workarounds for customer:
- set header `X-Redwood-Pool: novaai-gold` to force direct pool routing
- or modify SDK to send `X-Redwood-Tier: gold` (single string) instead of JSON array

becky_ops: tenant override applied at 09:18 UTC -> controlplane reports routing novaai -> novaai-gold. monitoring shows errors drop.

lina_support: customer confirmed improved latency and fewer 429s. sending initial update.

omar_runtime: root cause analysis: routing attempted to be permissive by parsing JSON arrays in the header, but the subsequent matching code expected a flat list of normalized alias strings. mismatch produced nested array token which didn't match canonical pool aliases. fix plan:
- hotfix: normalize parsed tiers to a flat list of strings (if parsed as array, expand; if parsed as string, split on commas; trim and lowercase) + defensive checks if parse returns nested arrays (est 2h).
- add unit tests covering header forms: `\"gold\"`, `gold,canary`, `[\"gold\"]`, `\"[\"gold\",\"canary\"]\"` and malformed inputs.
- add integration smoke that sends permuted header shapes and asserts routing hits tenant pool and autoscaler metrics.

omar_runtime: implementation note: change `try { parsed = JSON.parse(tierHeader) } catch { parsed = tierHeader }` to a robust normalizer that flattens arrays and coerces non-strings. add guards to never pass nested arrays to matcher.

maya_product: mark incident high priority. CSM will ask for credits for affected window; billing please evaluate.

chris_billing: noted. I'll pull logs and propose credit window once we have exact hit counts for 09:05-09:18 UTC.

kevin_sre: after hotfix we should run a noisy-neighbor simulation: high QPS from other tenants on shared-overflow and verify autoscaler on novaai-gold responds when routed traffic arrives.

sre-bot: :white_check_mark: incident INC-2026-915-tier-header-json-array-routing (severity: high) created  assignees: omar_runtime, becky_ops, kevin_sre

lina_support: keeping thread open until PR merges, canary completes, and billing decision closed. thanks everyone.
